title: Introduction to phylorug
text: Phylogenetic trees represent best-supported, statistically convincing hypotheses evolutionary history, ground truths (Steenwyk et al. 2023). Modern phylogenomic studies routinely produce multiple trees set taxa. Different data types (UCEs, transcriptomes, whole genomes), different analytical strategies (concatenation, coalescent methods, site-heterogeneous models), different inference software (IQ-TREE, ASTRAL, MrBayes) yield tree slightly different topology support values format. time, single tree inference method proven -rounder immune sources error. Incomplete lineage sorting, long-branch attraction, model misspecification, compositional heterogeneity affect different methods differently (Fleming et al. 2023). Accouringly, exploring multiple strategeies , different data types different infrence pipelines way researchers detect nodes may artifacts particular analytical choice versus nodes hold regardless method. question every node : clade appear analyses, strongly one support ? Answering flipping tree files tedious, error-prone, scale. phylorug solves drawing compact coloured grid rug every internal node reference tree(backbone). cell represents one tree, colour shows whether tree recovered clade strongly supported .

title: Introduction to phylorug
text: Giribet (2003) drew distinction motivates two modes phylorug. Nodal support measures confident single analysis clade bootstrap, posterior probability, LPP. Nodal stability measures whether clade consistently recovered across different analytical strategies, data types, inference methods ,extending Wheeler’s (1995) parameter-space sensitivity analysis framework. can decouple: clade may receive 100% bootstrap one model yet collapse others, carry 30–50% support everywhere yet appear every tree. phylorug shows . presence mode, node gets black dot every analysis recovers clade (stable) rug showing analyses recover . support mode, contested nodes receive rug cell gives quantitative visual support value analysis , just presence absence, strongly clade endorsed. Stable nodes receive black dot default. Setting rug_on_identical = TRUE extends rug universally recovered nodes well, revealing cases clade stable across analyses analyses support weakly.

title: Introduction to phylorug
text: rug plot concept originated Wheeler (1995), plotted clade recovery across gap transversion–transition cost ratios parsimony analysis direct optimization (POY). Giribet (2003) named plots “Navajo rugs” showed nodal support nodal stability can tell different stories. Sanders (2010) automated clade detection Cladescan (Perl), Machado (2015) extended approach YBYRÁ (Python), added topological distance calculation rogue taxon detection alongside sensitivity analysis. tools produce individual SVG plots per node must manually placed onto tree vector editor. Cladescan longer available online, YBYRÁ archived developer longer maintained. importantly, designed around sensitivity analysis within single analytical framework — varying parameters cost schemes — rather comparing trees fundamentally different inference pipelines report support incompatible formats (e.g., UFBoot2, SH-aLRT, posterior probability, ASTRAL LPP). phylorug extends lineage R. reads trees pipeline, bins support values metric-specific thresholds rather rescaling numerically, draws rugs directly reference tree — manual placement, external software.

title: Introduction to phylorug
text: Lets switch support mode see strongly tree supports clade. Cells shaded binned support strength, darker means stronger. Support values binned thresholds specific metric: tree LPP 0.95 tree LPP 0.65 compared LPP thresholds, tree carrying UFBoot2 values binned UFBoot2 thresholds independently. phylorug never cross-compares values different support metrics, LPP 0.95 UFBoot2 95 measure thing despite looking numerically quite similar can tempting convert dividing. support_type argument tells phylorug support metric tree uses, correct thresholds applied. IQ-TREE UFBoot2 values 0–100 scale; ASTRAL local posterior probabilities 0–1 scale. Define reuse across plot calls:
code: support_type <- c(    "70p_ASTRAL_partition_entropy" = "lpp",    "70p_ASTRAL_uce"               = "lpp",    "70p_ghost"                    = "ufboot",    "70p_partition_entropy"        = "ufboot"    ) plot_phylorug(    backbone, npm,    mode         = "support",    support_type = support_type  )

title: Introduction to phylorug
text: plot carries two legends. position legend (top-left) maps numbered cell tree.example, cell 1 first tree, cell 2 second, . threshold legend (top-right, support mode ) shows shade means. node see one patterns: Black dot: analyses recover clade unanimously (dot_identical = TRUE, default). rug drawn reduce clutter. Mixed grid: cells filled solid black, white. interesting nodes, position legend tells analysis agrees disagrees. -white grid: comparison tree recovers backbone clade. exists backbone topology. Setting hide_unsupported = TRUE removes -white rugs cleaner figure. node neither dot rug signals clade found backbone. support mode, filled cells use greyscale gradient plus two special colours. Black high support (e.g., UFBoot >= 95, LPP >= 0.95), dark grey high, light grey moderate, yellow low support. White means clade recovered. Red means clade recovered carries computable support value.

code: # Build the plotting input from real trees: backbone <- sample_trees[["70p_uce"]] others   <- sample_trees[names(sample_trees) != "70p_uce"] npm <- node_presence_matrix(backbone, others, support_col = 1)  # --- Presence mode -------------------------------------------------------- # Each cell shows whether an analysis recovered the backbone clade. # Writing to a file uses the internal scaling engine for a clean figure. tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".pdf") plot_phylorug(backbone, npm, file = tmp) #> Warning: for '1 – 70p_ASTRAL_partition_entropy' in 'mbcsToSbcs': - substituted for – (U+2013) #> Warning: for '2 – 70p_ASTRAL_uce' in 'mbcsToSbcs': - substituted for – (U+2013) #> Warning: for '3 – 70p_ghost' in 'mbcsToSbcs': - substituted for – (U+2013) #> Warning: for '4 – 70p_partition_entropy' in 'mbcsToSbcs': - substituted for – (U+2013) unlink(tmp)  # --- Support mode --------------------------------------------------------- # Cells are shaded by support strength. `support_type` tells plot_phylorug # how to read each tree's values: ASTRAL trees carry local posterior # probability ("lpp"), IQ-TREE trees carry UFBoot2 ("ufboot"). support_type <- c(   "70p_ASTRAL_partition_entropy" = "lpp",   "70p_ASTRAL_uce"               = "lpp",   "70p_ghost"                    = "ufboot",   "70p_partition_entropy"        = "ufboot" ) tmp2 <- tempfile(fileext = ".pdf") plot_phylorug(backbone, npm,               file         = tmp2,               mode         = "support",               support_idx  = 1,               support_type = support_type) #> Warning: for '1 – 70p_ASTRAL_partition_entropy' in 'mbcsToSbcs': - substituted for – (U+2013) #> Warning: for '2 – 70p_ASTRAL_uce' in 'mbcsToSbcs': - substituted for – (U+2013) #> Warning: for '3 – 70p_ghost' in 'mbcsToSbcs': - substituted for – (U+2013) #> Warning: for '4 – 70p_partition_entropy' in 'mbcsToSbcs': - substituted for – (U+2013) unlink(tmp2)  # --- Some optional controls ----------------------------------------------- # include_backbone = TRUE adds the backbone as its own cell in every rug; # rug_position = "outside" places grids toward the tips instead of the crook; # hide_unsupported = TRUE leaves clades no analysis recovered bare. tmp3 <- tempfile(fileext = ".pdf") plot_phylorug(backbone, npm,               file             = tmp3,               include_backbone = TRUE,               rug_position     = "outside") #> Warning: for '1 – backbone' in 'mbcsToSbcs': - title: Trim the backbone and its comparison trees to their shared set of taxa — prune_to_shared
code: # Build a backbone and comparison trees that do NOT all share the same taxa, # so there is something to trim. (In practice these come from read_trees().) backbone <- ape::read.tree(   text = "((((A,B),(C,D)),((E,F),(G,H))),(I,J));" ) others <- list(   # All ten taxa, same as the backbone:   tree_1 = ape::read.tree(text = "((((A,B),(C,D)),((E,F),(G,H))),(I,J));"),   # Missing J:   tree_2 = ape::read.tree(text = "((((A,B),(C,D)),((E,F),(G,H))),I);"),   # Missing I:   tree_3 = ape::read.tree(text = "((((A,B),(C,D)),((E,F),(G,H))),J);") )  # See which taxa are missing, and from which trees, before trimming: check_taxa(backbone, others) #> 2 comparison tree(s) are MISSING backbone taxa: tree_2, tree_3. Any backbone clade containing a missing taxon cannot be evaluated in those trees. Use `prune_to_shared()` to reduce the backbone and the comparison trees to their common taxa. See `attr(result, "diagnostics")` for the taxa involved. #> [1] FALSE #> attr(,"diagnostics") #>   comparison  status n_taxa missing extra #> 1     tree_2 missing      9       J       #> 2     tree_3 missing      9       I        # Trim the backbone and every comparison tree to their shared taxa: shared <- prune_to_shared(backbone, others) #> Dropped 2 of 10 taxa, leaving 8: I, J. Any clade containing a dropped taxon can no longer be reported.  # Which taxa were dropped: attr(shared, "dropped") #> [1] "I" "J"  # The pruned trees are ready for node_presence_matrix(): shared$backbone #>  #> Phylogenetic tree with 8 tips and 7 internal nodes. #>  #> Tip labels: #>   A, B, C, D, E, F, ... #>  #> Rooted; no branch length. shared$trees #> $tree_1 #>  #> Phylogenetic tree with 8 tips and 7 internal nodes. #>  #> Tip labels: #>   A, B, C, D, E, F, ... #>  #> Rooted; no branch length. #>  #> $tree_2 #>  #> Phylogenetic tree with 8 tips and 7 internal nodes. #>  #> Tip labels: #>   A, B, C, D, E, F, ... #>  #> Rooted; no branch length. #>  #> $tree_3 #>  #> Phylogenetic tree with 8 tips and 7 internal nodes. #>  #> Tip labels: #>   A, B, C, D, E, F, ... #>  #> Rooted; no branch length. #>

code: # phylorug ships example  raw tree files in its `extdata` directory. # Point read_trees() at one of those folders: dir <- system.file("extdata", "beetles_70p", package = "phylorug")  # With only the directory, read_trees() detects each file's format from its # contents (NEXUS or Newick, the two formats this version supports) and # matches the default extension filter (tre, tree, treefile, nwk, ...).  trees <- read_trees(dir) #> Read 5 analyses (5 trees) from: /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/phylorug/extdata/beetles_70p  # The result is a named list, one element per analysis, ready to pass to # [check_taxa()] or [node_presence_matrix()]:  names(trees) #> [1] "70p_ASTRAL_partition_entropy" "70p_ASTRAL_uce"               #> [3] "70p_ghost"                    "70p_partition_entropy"        #> [5] "70p_uce"                       # If a folder holds many files and you want only some, narrow `ext` # to one extension, or to a set of them: trees <- read_trees(dir, ext = "tre") #> Read 5 analyses (5 trees) from: /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/phylorug/extdata/beetles_70p trees <- read_trees(dir, ext = c("tre", "tree", "treefile")) #> Read 5 analyses (5 trees) from: /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/phylorug/extdata/beetles_70p  # For full control you can also force a single parser. Note this applies # one format to every matched file, so a file of a different format would # not be read. trees <- read_trees(dir, format = "newick") #> Read 5 analyses (5 trees) from: /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/phylorug/extdata/beetles_70p

title: Relabel tips across a list of trees using a lookup table — translate_tips
code: # Example trees and a lookup table ship inside phylorug, so we first read # them into the environment, then tell translate_tips() which column holds # the current labels and which holds the replacements: dir  <- system.file("extdata", "beetles_50p", package = "phylorug") file <- system.file("extdata", "beetles_50p", "biogeo.csv", package = "phylorug")  trees <- read_trees(dir) #> Read 5 analyses (5 trees) from: /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/phylorug/extdata/beetles_50p dict  <- utils::read.csv(file)  # Relabel tips from specimen codes to species names. The message reports how # many tips were translated and how many were left unchanged in each tree: translated <- translate_tips(trees, dict,                              from_col = "specimen_code",                              to_col   = "species_name") #> 50p_ASTRAL_partition_entropy: 316 tips translated, 0 unchanged #> 50p_ASTRAL_uce: 316 tips translated, 0 unchanged #> 50p_ghost: 316 tips translated, 0 unchanged #> 50p_partition_entropy: 316 tips translated, 0 unchanged #> 50p_uce: 316 tips translated, 0 unchanged
